# ===========================================================================
# THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE TAG SET -- TWO TIERS, AND THE DIFFERENCE
# BETWEEN THEM IS A HARD API LIMIT, NOT AN EDITORIAL CHOICE.
# ===========================================================================
#
# TIER 1 -- [TOPICS]. GitHub repo topics. Capped at TWENTY by the server; the
#   API rejects the 21st. Nothing we write here changes that. These are the
#   structured, browsable tags: each becomes a crawlable github.com/topics/<t>
#   page, which is the highest-value surface we have.
#
# TIER 2 -- [SIGNATURE]. The README signature block. **NO LIMIT.** This is
#   visible markdown text, and visible text is what was MEASURED to survive
#   GitHub's sanitizer intact (POST api.github.com/markdown: <meta> deleted,
#   display:none stripped-but-rendered, plain "#tag" text survives verbatim).
#   This is the true descendant of the forum signature, and it is where an
#   unlimited tag set belongs. Put everything true here.
#
# The 20-cap applies ONLY to tier 1. Capping tier 2 at 20 would be throwing
# away the one surface that has no cap.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE RULE THAT GOVERNS BOTH TIERS: every tag must name something that is
# GENUINELY PRESENT. tag-manager.yml enforces this mechanically for tier 2 by
# scanning the actual trees of both accounts -- Saimonokuma and
# Nova-Violet-Role -- and refusing any tag it cannot find evidence for. That is
# why "unlimited" is safe here: the generator cannot invent a tag, so a longer
# list is a more complete description rather than a bigger lie.
#
# Measured 2026-07-31 via the public API:
#   Saimonokuma       Chaos-SymbioseOS (C) - GHC-COMPILER-PYTHON (Python)
#                     MultiLinkExtractor- - skills (Python)
#   Nova-Violet-Role  .github - claude-rolling-context-Lean-4- (Python)
# Tier 2 draws from these plus this repo's own tree. A tag naming a language or
# a subject that appears in NEITHER account is a defect and fails the job.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ===========================================================================
# TIER 3 -- [PROPERTIES]. GitHub ORG CUSTOM PROPERTIES.
# ===========================================================================
#
# Topics are free-text and crawlable; custom properties are a SCHEMA, defined
# once at the organisation level and given a value per repository. They are
# what an org uses to answer "which of our repos are actually verified" without
# reading forty READMEs.
#
# THE RULE THAT MATTERS HERE, and it is the same one that governs every theorem
# in this repository: A PROPERTY MUST NOT BE A SNAPSHOT THAT EXPIRES.
#
#   verify-command = bash checker/gate-all.sh --full     <- durable: an
#       INSTRUMENT. Still true after the hundredth theorem is added.
#   theorem-count  = 100                                 <- REJECTED, and this
#       is why the field does not exist: it is false the day someone proves
#       one more, and the obvious repair is to stop updating it. A number that
#       nothing re-derives is a claim, not a fact.
#
# `platforms` follows the same discipline in the other direction: it lists
# linux and windows because CI RAN there and went green (run 30684381090,
# 2026-08-01), and it omits macos because nothing has ever tested macos. The
# day a macos job passes, the value moves -- not before.
#
# Format: name = value   (multi_select values are comma-separated)
# Applied and verified by .github/workflows/tag-manager.yml, which needs the
# API; checker/tags-consistency.sh checks the STRUCTURE locally, with no token.

[PROPERTIES]
verification = machine-checked-lean4
project-kind = claude-code-plugin
licence-model = agpl-3.0-or-eupl-1.2
maintenance = actively-developed
org-role = flagship
verify-command = bash checker/gate-all.sh --full
platforms = linux,windows
